# Add and Remove Elements From Queue

#### Course: Learn C++ STL

## Add and Remove Elements From Queue

In this section, we will look at the following functions:

- push() - inserts an element to the rear of the queue
- pop() - removes an element from the front of the queue

For example,

```cpp
1#include <iostream>
2#include <queue>
3
4using namespace std;
5
6int main(){
7
8    // Create a queue of integers
9    queue<int> numbers;
10
11    // Add elements to the rear of the queue
12    numbers.push(1);
13    numbers.push(2);
14    numbers.push(3);
15
16    // numbers = {1, 2, 3}
17
18    // Remove an element from the front of the queue
19    numbers.pop();
20
21    // numbers = {2, 3}
22
23    return 0;
24}
```

![Idea Emoji](data:image/png;base64,)

Here, we have used the push() function to insert elements to the rear of the queue:

```cpp
numbers.push(1);
numbers.push(2);
numbers.push(3);
```

After this operation, the numbers queue will consist of the elements 1, 2, and 3.

Then, we have removed one element from the front of the queue using the pop() function

```cpp
numbers.pop();
```

This will remove the first element that we inserted to the queue i.e. 1.
